description: Cases every host of FormLogic's Python contract must agree on (formlogic/ui/src/lib/formlogic/python/pythonContract.ts).
kind: flow (logic_block: one expression, else statements setting `result`), condition (one expression, Python truthiness), applogic (run(ctx)), syntax (compile only).

context: the evaluation's context object. expect: {ok: true, value} compared as JSON; {threw: <regex>} a guest error (syntax, raise, runtime) whose message matches; {resource: <regex>} an engine limit whose message matches.
Every host runs these against whatever ZIPP web-python release it installs; a change in ZIPP's Python frontend shows up here as a diff.

cases.note: Implicit line joining inside the expression wrapper makes the second line a call on the first. It fails loudly; write statements and set result instead.

cases.source:
c = next((r for r in nodes["customers"] if r["answers"]["phone"] == inputs["from"]), None)
result = {"found": c is not None, "name": c["answers"]["name"] if c else None}

cases.note: Context values are plain dicts: subscript them (inputs["durationSeconds"]).

cases.source: [validators.email("a@b.co"), compliance.tfnValid("123-456-789"), finance.transferFee(1000, "Schwab"), safety.riskLevel(12), is_empty("  "), is_not_empty([1]), contains([1, 2], 2), avg([1, 2, 3])]

cases.note: Checked by name lookup: in ZIPP v0.0.18 globals() inside an imported module returns the entry module's globals.
A ZIPP v0.0.18 defect: assigning another module's attribute raises. The contract binds names with `global` inside formlogic.py and never depends on it. A fix in ZIPP changes this case.

cases.source:
import formlogic
result = [formlogic._plain(float("nan")) is None, formlogic._plain(float("inf")) is None, formlogic._plain(-float("inf")) is None, formlogic._plain(1.5)]
cases.note: ZIPP also projects non-finite floats to null; _plain does it in the guest so every host agrees before the value crosses.

cases.source:
v = 1
for i in range(40):
    v = [v]
result = v
cases.note: ZIPP v0.0.18 carries at most 32 levels across the host boundary; deeper results fail there.

cases.source:
v = 1
for i in range(70):
    v = [v]
result = v

line = "x" * 1000
for i in range(9000):
    print(line)
result = "quiet"
cases.note: print is a no-op, so printing never reaches the engine's output limits. (sys.stdout.write is not covered: in ZIPP v0.0.18 a few thousand writes without a newline trap the engine.)
ZIPP v0.0.18 reports a runtime error inside a multi-line expression at the line the expression starts on.
